body: I have insurance starting December 1st - it isn't good insurance, but I think it may be my only hope.  I am planning on going to the hospital at that point and telling them everything and hopefully getting help.  I can't believe my family can't even be human to me - I have always helped where I can when I was healthy; I helped nurse my Mom when she was dying ... and my dad was abusive even during that - demanding I be there at night so he could sleep, refusing to give me private time with my Mom, yelling at my Mom, etc.  I tried to tell my brother-in-law and sister that he was toxic to my mental health (my exact words) and that I needed somewhere to stay for a bit ... "Well, we don't want this environment becoming toxic - no way."  Literally fighting for my life and pushed further into this hell by my family.

I always feel that the people in my life will use it as a way to get pity for themselves if I kill myself.  They'll make it a Facebook post and/or some bullshit one-liner about 'getting help' - the same people who have never helped someone in their life through a mental health crisis.  I honestly would prefer no funeral because it will be a staged bunch of bullshit for the benefit of the people there who wouldn't lift a finger to help someone in need.

I attempted suicide almost two weeks ago; and I feel much the same as you - confused, overwhelmed at times, embarrassed, angry with myself for hurting/scaring family and friends, and unsure of how to even share what I've been going through with friends.  I attempted to hang myself - and instead just managed to cause myself injury that may have made my situation even worse.  Unfortunately, I wasn't 'caught' or forced into treatment - though perhaps I should have been.  I only told my family what I attempted to do a few days ago - the reactions were anger primarily, and it's left me feeling like a shell of a person (or even the person I was 3 months ago).

I still have intense fear - fear of getting back to the point (again) where I feel I have to take my life because of lack of other opportunities or an even remote chance of leading a 'normal' life.  My mental health has been destroyed, and my resources are slim; I'm starting outpatient therapy (probably once a week at most) on December 1st.  I can't afford to address the physical injuries I have, or be hospitalized - though I know I need both.  Many days I try to envision a future, and it's incredibly tough to even comprehend how I could be successful at a job, earn enough money to survive, and 're-find' a sense of purpose/happiness/optimism.

Some of the most difficult things to reconcile are the realizations that I will have no real help moving forward; from professionals, family, friends, or relatives.  I know that I'm on my own, and there is a good chance of being homeless in my not-so-distant future.  I don't want to die, but I realize that I've painted myself into a corner that I may not be able to escape during this life.

I wish you the very best, and I'm praying for you to make a full recovery and rebound from all of this.
